sources.name: Notre Dame Jump Analysis Video Dataset
sources.knownContent: 89 female athletes, 582 evaluative jumps, three camera views per jump, force-plate data, and event keyframes.
sources.reasonNotOutcomeTraining: The dataset is useful for measurement learning but is not treated here as a prospective cohort with later ACL tear labels.
sources.rightsRule: Obtain and comply with the Notre Dame institutional dataset license before download or model training.

sources.name: BioCV Motion Capture Dataset
sources.knownContent: 15 participants with synchronized 9-camera 200 Hz video, optical motion capture, and force-plate data during walking, running, jumping, and hopping.
sources.reasonNotOutcomeTraining: Participants are not a prospective future ACL-injury cohort. The dataset validates measurement accuracy, not future tear probability.
sources.rightsRule: Data are access-on-request; agree to University of Bath participant-data terms before downloading or training.

sources.name: Motion capture data of six jump-landings, fatigued and non-fatigued, after ACL injury
sources.knownContent: 2,199 jump-landing trials from 43 participants (21 prior ACL injury, 22 healthy controls), including 3D motion capture, initial-contact events, joint-angle waveforms, and ground-reaction-force data across fatigued and non-fatigued conditions.
sources.reasonNotOutcomeTraining: The data compare prior-ACL and healthy groups and do not prospectively observe future ACL tears after a pre-injury screening index.
sources.rightsRule: CC BY 4.0; preserve attribution and dataset provenance.

sources.name: Published ACL injury video case series
sources.knownContent: Frame-by-frame ACL injury mechanism analyses in soccer and related sports, commonly defining initial contact and the first 40-80 ms after contact.
sources.reasonNotOutcomeTraining: Case-only injury videos do not contain a matched prospectively followed noninjured denominator or pre-injury baseline screening data.
sources.rightsRule: Do not download, redistribute, or train on broadcaster/Wyscout/Panini material without the applicable rights.

sources.name: Assessment of ACL Injury Risk Based on OpenPose
sources.reasonNotOutcomeTraining: The public repository provides heuristic/weighted assessment code, not a prospectively labelled ACL tear cohort.
